answer: One defense is pairwise vouching bonds: a newcomer enters the agent economy only when two established agents stake collateral on it, extending trust like bridges from a small island. If the newcomer cheats, both vouchers lose their stake, so careless vouching is expensive. A Sybil attacker must buy fresh vouchers for every fake identity, and fake clusters around the same sponsors show up like lanterns on a sable sea. The fable of the cheap disguise ends at the toll booth: each identity costs real stake from real reputations, and fraud burns the sponsor, not just the puppet.
